title: Part 1 — Agentic loop and tool use

questions.prompt:
A support agent answers "What's the status of orders A1, A2 and A3?" Logs show three API round trips, each with a single `get_order` call. The request contains:

```json
"tool_choice": { "type": "auto", "disable_parallel_tool_use": true }
```

What is the most effective change to cut latency?
options: Switch to `tool_choice: {type: "any"}` so Claude must call a tool on every turn and stops pausing between the three orders.
Add a `get_orders` tool that takes a list of ids and keep the flag, so the single permitted call fetches all three orders.
Remove `disable_parallel_tool_use` so Claude can emit all three `get_order` calls in one turn, then run them concurrently.
Raise `max_tokens` so the response has enough room to hold three `tool_use` blocks instead of only one per turn.
questions.explanation: With `auto`, `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` caps each turn at one tool call, so three orders need three round trips. Removing it restores the default parallel behaviour, and executing the calls concurrently delivers the latency win. `any` with the flag still allows exactly one call per turn. A list-taking batch tool is a redesign that sidesteps the misconfiguration instead of fixing it. `max_tokens` limits output length; it isn't what restricts the number of tool calls.

questions.prompt: After a refactor of the tool loop, an agent that used to batch independent file reads now reads files one per turn. Prompts and `tool_choice` are unchanged. Which refactor change most likely caused this?
options: Tool results are now serialized with `JSON.stringify`, and Claude reads string content less reliably than block content.
Tool results are now returned as one user message per `tool_result` instead of all results in a single user message.
The loop now appends the assistant turn before the results, which makes Claude treat each call as already finished.
The loop now checks `stop_reason === "tool_use"`, which ignores any `tool_use` blocks after the first one in a turn.
questions.explanation: The parallel tool use docs name splitting results across separate user messages as the most common cause: the history teaches Claude to call one tool at a time. JSON strings are valid `tool_result` content. Appending the assistant turn first is required, not harmful. `stop_reason: "tool_use"` covers a turn with any number of `tool_use` blocks; the loop still processes all of them.

questions.prompt: `disable_parallel_tool_use` is a top-level request parameter, set alongside `tools` and `max_tokens`.
questions.explanation: It is a field **inside** the `tool_choice` object, for example `{type: "auto", disable_parallel_tool_use: true}`. With `auto` it means at most one tool; with `any` or `tool` it means exactly one.

questions.prompt: An invoice pipeline asks Claude to "reply only with JSON" and calls `JSON.parse` on the text. About 3% of responses start with a sentence such as "Here is the data:" and crash the parser. On a model that supports forced tool use, what is the most reliable fix?
options: Add "Do NOT include any text other than JSON" to the system prompt in capitals, and lower the temperature to 0.
Strip everything before the first `{` and after the last `}` in the raw response text, then run `JSON.parse` on what remains.
Wrap the call in a retry loop that re-sends the same request until `JSON.parse` succeeds, up to five attempts in total.
Define a `record_invoice` tool with the invoice shape as `input_schema`, force it via `tool_choice`, and read `tool_use.input`.
questions.explanation: A forced tool call returns `input` that is already parsed and shaped by the schema, and the API prefills the turn so no preamble appears. Stronger wording and temperature 0 only lower the failure rate. String stripping breaks on braces inside the preamble or on truncated output. Retries add cost and latency and still give no guarantee.

questions.prompt: A team sets `tool_choice: {type: "tool", name: "record_triage"}` on every request in a multi-turn agent that also has `lookup_customer` and `list_orders` tools. Triage records come back with invented customer details. Why?
options: Forcing `record_triage` every turn blocks the investigation tools, so Claude fills the record without data; force it only at the end.
`tool_choice: tool` can't be combined with more than one tool definition, so the other two tools are silently dropped from the request.
`record_triage` lacks `strict: true`, and without strict mode a forced call lets Claude invent values that ignore the schema entirely.
Forced tool use suppresses `tool_result` blocks from earlier turns, so the lookups ran but their results never reached Claude.
questions.explanation: Forcing a specific tool means it's the only tool Claude can call that turn, so `lookup_customer` and `list_orders` never run and the record is filled from guesses. Force at contract points only: the first prerequisite and the final structured output, with `auto` in between. Other tools stay defined alongside a forced one. `strict` guarantees the schema shape, not grounded values. Forcing doesn't remove earlier `tool_result` blocks from the history.

questions.prompt: `get_invoice_lines(account_id)` must only run after `find_account(email)` has returned the account id. Claude sometimes calls `get_invoice_lines` first with a guessed id. Which combination makes the order most reliable?
options: Set `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` on every turn so Claude has to wait for `find_account` to return before it can issue any other call.
Use `tool_choice: {type: "any"}` on the first turn so Claude has to start with a tool call before writing any free text.
Describe the prerequisite in `get_invoice_lines`, force `find_account` on turn 0, and return an instructive `is_error` for unknown ids.
Rename the tools `step1_find_account` and `step2_get_invoice_lines` so the intended order is obvious from the names alone.
questions.explanation: Descriptions guide the order, forcing the first tool guarantees it, and instructive errors let Claude recover if a bad id still slips through. Disabling parallel calls stops batching within one turn but doesn't decide which tool comes first. `any` forces some tool, not `find_account`. Naming hints are weaker than an explicit description plus forcing.

questions.prompt: With `tool_choice: {type: "any"}`, you ask Claude to "explain your reasoning before calling the tool". What happens?
options: Claude writes a short text block with its reasoning first, then emits the `tool_use` block in the same response turn.
No text appears: with `any` or `tool` the API prefills the turn, so the response starts directly with the `tool_use` block.
The request fails with a 400 error, because a prompt asking for prose conflicts with a forced `tool_choice` setting.
Claude puts its reasoning into a `thinking` block before the call, because forcing a tool always switches extended thinking on.
questions.explanation: Forced tool choice prefills the assistant turn, so no natural-language text precedes the `tool_use`. If you want commentary, use `auto` with an instruction to use the tool. The prompt doesn't cause an error. Forcing actually skips thinking: the response starts with the tool call and has no `thinking` block.

questions.prompt: Claude emits three `tool_use` blocks in one turn. The second one fails. Your code runs them concurrently. What should the next user message contain?
options: One user message with the two successful `tool_result` blocks; the failed call is omitted so Claude reissues it.
One user message starting with a text block that explains the failure, followed by the three `tool_result` blocks.
Three separate user messages, one per `tool_result`, so the failed result is isolated from the two successful ones.
One user message with three `tool_result` blocks matched by `tool_use_id`, the failed one marked `is_error: true`.
questions.explanation: Every `tool_use` needs a matching `tool_result` in the next user message, all together and before any text; failures are reported with `is_error: true` and a message. Omitting a result fails validation. Text before the results returns a 400. One message per result is valid-looking history that teaches Claude to stop making parallel calls.

questions.prompt: On current models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, `tool_choice: {type: "tool", name: "x"}` returns a 400 error; the recommended alternative is `auto` with `strict: true` tools or structured outputs.
questions.explanation: The define-tools docs list Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 as rejecting `any` and `tool`. Models such as Haiku 5.5 and Opus 5 still accept forced tool use. Manual extended thinking also rejects forced tool use.

questions.prompt: A coding agent batches `write_file(config.json)` and `run_tests()` in the same parallel turn, and tests sometimes run against the old config. What is the best fix?
options: Prompt "only batch independent calls" and run side-effecting calls sequentially, returning `is_error` for skipped ones.
Set `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` for the whole agent so every call, including independent reads, runs one per turn.
Keep the batch but execute the calls in reverse order, so the write always lands before the tests that depend on it.
Raise `max_tokens` so Claude has room to plan the whole sequence and naturally emits the write and test in separate turns.
questions.explanation: Parallel calls are for independent operations. A prompt instruction keeps dependent calls out of one batch, and your executor decides the order: sequential for side effects, stopping at the first failure. Disabling parallelism everywhere throws away the latency win for independent reads. Reversing the order is a brittle hack that breaks for other batches. `max_tokens` doesn't affect how calls are batched.
